'''Rawle Junior Kalomo Marshall ''' (born February 20, 1982)<ref>[http://www.nba.com/draft2004/profiles/RawleMarshall.html Rawle Marshall 2004 Draft profile]</ref> is a Guyanese-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Shahrdari Gorgan BC|Shahrdari Gorgan]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].

==Early life==
Marshall is a 2000 graduate of [[Detroit]]'s [[Mackenzie High School (Michigan)|Mackenzie High School]], where he was [[salutatorian]] of his [[twelfth grade|senior]] class.

Marshall's favorite basketball player as a youth was [[Penny Hardaway]].<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/article/NBDL-Interview-Rawle-Marshall-1184/ NBDL Interview: Rawle Marshall]</ref>

==College career==
Marshall spent his college [[freshman]] season at [[Ball State University]], but then moved to [[Oakland University]] for his final three collegiate seasons. He was named [[The Summit League|Mid-Continent Conference]]'s Newcomer of the Year and Defensive Player of the Year during his sophomore season in 2002–03. During his senior season in 2004–05, he helped Oakland win its first Mid-Continent Conference title. Marshall was named [[Most Valuable Player]] of the tournament. His stats during his three years with Oakland were 18.6 points per game, 6.3 rebounds per game, 2.2 steals per game and 1.1 blocks per game. He also became [[Oakland University]]'s all-time leader in blocked shots in 90 games played.

==Professional career==

===NBA===

Not selected during the [[2005 NBA draft]], Marshall has participated in several [[NBA Summer League]]s (Southern California Summer Pro League with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Rocky Mountain Revue]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]). His performances (18.6 points per game, 3.0 rebounds per game and 1.4 assists per game in 27.4 minutes per game in the Rocky Mountain Revue) helped him to earn a one-year contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on August 5, 2005.

Marshall did not find the court much early in his rookie season with the Mavericks. Instead, Marshall was sent to the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] team the [[Fort Worth Flyers]], where he averaged 17.4 points per game. He then returned to the Dallas Mavericks, where he started multiple games due to injuries to [[Josh Howard]], [[Adrian Griffin]], and [[Devin Harris]]. While his minutes still were limited, he surpassed the expectations that surrounded an average undrafted rookie. However, he did not make the Mavericks' playoffs roster in 2006. On July 23, 2006, Marshall was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]], along with [[Darrell Armstrong]] and [[Josh Powell]], for [[Anthony Johnson (basketball)|Anthony Johnson]]. He spent the 2006–07 season with the Pacers.

===Europe and Asia===

Marshall played with the Serbian club [[KK Hemofarm]] during the 2007–08 season. He also played with Hemofarm in that season's [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] ([[European professional club basketball system|the 2nd tier European-wide competition]]) and the regional [[Adriatic League]]. He averaged 17.3 points per game in the EuroCup and 15.7 points per game in the Adriatic League. With his team Hemofarm he reached last 16 in EuroCup, where they lost to later finalist [[Akasvayu Girona]]. He was also finalist in Adriatic league and [[Basketball League of Serbia]], where in both cases Hemofarm was defeated by [[KK Partizan]].

He then moved to the [[A1 Liga|Croatian League]] club [[KK Cibona]] for the 2008–09 season, a club also of the regional Adriatic League and also of the top European-wide competition the [[EuroLeague]]. He was honored as the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round|EuroLeague Round 7 MVP]] during the 2008–09 season. He joined the [[LNB Pro A]] club [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] in 2009.<ref>[https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/breves2009/20091117_150051_marshall-signe-a-l-asvel.html R. Marshall signe à l'ASVEL] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100316104607/http://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/breves2009/20091117_150051_marshall-signe-a-l-asvel.html |date=2010-03-16 }}</ref> In August 2010 he joined [[PAOK BC|PAOK]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130122141512/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/75034/3735|title=Busy PAOK pens deal with Marshall}}</ref>

In July 2011, he signed with [[BC Astana]] in Kazakhstan.<ref>[https://www.asia-basket.com/Kazakhstan/basketball.aspx?NewsID=232212 BC Astana bring in Rawle Marshall]</ref> In October 2013, he signed with [[CSU Asesoft Ploiești]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CSU ASESOFT tabs Marshall |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/121485/8174/csu-asesoft-tabs-marshall |accessdate=January 28, 2014 |newspaper=Eurocupbasketball.com |date=October 28, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104160818/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/121485/8174/csu-asesoft-tabs-marshall |archivedate=November 4, 2014 }}</ref>

On December 7, 2014, Marshall signed with [[Koroivos B.C.|Koroivos Amaliadas]] of Greece.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rawle Marshall (ex Ploiesti) is a newcomer at Koroivos|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/385885|accessdate=December 9, 2014|work=Eurobasket.com|date=December 7, 2014}}</ref>
